postgres.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

diagnostics.note: Instrumented pool spans; query roundtrip includes network, server, decoding and JS scheduling. Warmup included.
Instrumented pool spans; query roundtrip includes network, server, decoding and JS scheduling. Warmup included.

semantics.shape: seven required root fields, three required nested fields; all four numbers bounded inclusively ±1000000
semantics.booleans: non-mutating boolean checks, no coercion/defaults/copy; loose permits extras, strict rejects root and nested extras; own plain enumerable JSON objects only
semantics.errorCost: Ajv boolean calls also maintain their normal first-error field; no detailed-error or throwing rankings
semantics.serialization: valid exact-shape finite plain JSON only; byte-equal property order and escapes; no validation/copy/getters/toJSON/excess-key or invalid-input equivalence claim
semantics.sink: rotating 32 input objects; every result contributes to checked checksum; serialized strings escape into retained ring

settings.load: closed loop maximum throughput; latency is not coordinated-omission corrected

fairness.nativeDrizzleStrategy: One lateral JSON aggregation query, native row mapper. Other graph lanes issue three batched queries.
fairness.builderBoundary: The pg/Drizzle/Kysely/zmdb-builder lanes use common pg transport and manual graph assembly; repository and deferred use the actual public repository.
fairness.timing: Clean intervals include latency-array allocation, consistently across lanes; CPU profiles omit those arrays.

httpBodyAblation.interpretation: One diagnostic only: announced and post-read size checks preserved, early bounded streaming enforcement not preserved. It retains the existing body-null getter check; no claim that full native request parsing or the wider Fetch gap has been isolated.

httpProfiles.interpretation: These are sampled intervals, not a measured hardware CPU-time ledger. Non-idle includes warmup and response checks (Node also startup); saved profiles do not mark the clean timed interval, so hot-only CPU time is not claimed.

These are sampled intervals, not a measured hardware CPU-time ledger. Non-idle includes warmup and response checks (Node also startup); saved profiles do not mark the clean timed interval, so hot-only CPU time is not claimed.

httpBodyNoGetterAblation.interpretation: Diagnostic only; early streaming size enforcement lost. The body-null getter is removed; null/empty bodies still map to undefined through the existing zero-byte check. Sample ranges must be considered; this four-cell probe alone does not establish a production improvement.
httpBodyNoGetterAblation.controlLimit: The final control is the original bounded reader, not the native-reader-with-getter variant. The13.4% result measures the combined native-reader/no-eager-getter diagnostic, not the isolated effect of the getter alone. Do not compare the two sessions as if temperature/runtime state were fixed.

limitations: One development laptop with ordinary desktop services still running; no universal winner is established.
HTTP is closed-loop throughput; p99 is not corrected for coordinated omission or an open-loop SLO.
Index comparison is zmdb versus itself, not an advantage applied against unindexed peers.
Profile shares are observations, not independently additive speedups.
Trace instrumentation perturbs timing; it is excluded from clean rankings.
All ablations are unshipped diagnostics. The native body-reader ablations lose early streaming memory-limit enforcement.
No TLS, multicore HTTP, remote DB, ORM on Bun/Deno, large bodies, wide unions/arrays or all frameworks/dialects were measured.
